why: a replayed session_id awarding a second time. The whole reward commit is ONE exclusive transaction keyed by session_id, so a ceremony re-entered after a kill — the retry a flaky write forces, or a learner backgrounding at S1a and coming back — must decide to apply NOTHING the second time. Without it every kill during a ceremony is a coin flip on the learner's rewards.

cases.name: a first commit applies exactly the outcome, inventing and dropping nothing
the falsifier: replaying the SAME session_id applies nothing at all
and it is the id that decides, not the position: a mid-ledger collision still refuses
a DIFFERENT session still commits while others sit on the ledger
a zero-value outcome is still a commit, not a null: 0 XP is a decision

mustNotBe: a non-null plan for any already-committed session_id, or a plan whose xp/gems differ from the outcome it was handed.
addedNote: Added at P1 integration: INV-CER-01 is a P0 id that shipped with tests and no falsifying input.
